positions.name: GateAsSecurityMandate
positions.frame: why is the signed-manifest gate mandatory, and how far does that necessity reach?
positions.why: Across register, relational, and value readings these four expressions perform the same move: a mandatory precondition (src-1, restated as a labeled clause in src-3) grounded in a cited past failure (src-2) and extended to cover every environment (src-4). Value marks all four with the same conservation/competence appeal — security and process integrity as the governing good — while register and relational readings show src-1/src-3/src-4 sharing the authority-ranking, labeled-clause performance and src-2 supplying the justificatory ground that performance leans on. The set holds a mild tension: src-2 is plain-spoken and evidentiary where src-1/src-3/src-4 are formal and declarative, but the frame reads that tension as cause-and-effect within one mandate, not as competing positions.
